title: Orchestrated Regional Routing Adjudicator — latency SLOs, geo-pin overrides, capacity-aware shedding
creator: Liam Chen
description: Goal: Implement a top-level "Orchestrated Regional Routing Adjudicator (ORRA)" that mediates request routing across regions using a combination of latency SLOs, explicit geo-pin overrides, and capacity-aware shedding. ORRA will be the canonical decision point for selecting a target region or model variant for a given request, emitting rich signals for observability and triggering circuit-breakers and shedding when necessary.
acceptance_criteria: ORRA returns a routing decision within 2ms p50 for local evaluation path
Requests are routed to a pinned region when customer has active geo-pin flag (respecting tenant isolation) unless pinned region is in degraded state and override policy is configured
When regional capacity falls below the configured soft threshold, ORRA triggers priority-based shedding and returns configured degraded response or fallback model variant
Circuit-breaker transitions are visible in Console dashboards and produce alerts when regional error rate > 5% for 1 minute
Canary rollout of ORRA (10% traffic) with automatic rollback on error SLI regression
comments: 2026-02-12 - Kickoff: scoped MVP to support three primitives: latency-SLO scoring, geo-pin enforcement, and capacity-score fallbacks. Liam: initial PRD posted.
2026-02-17 - Design review: PM and SRE prefer soft-shed first (return lighter model) before hard drop. Agreed to implement two-mode shedding: graceful and immediate.
2026-02-22 - Prototype: latency scoring function implemented in local simulator; p95 evaluation aligns with expected 3ms decision CPU cost. Added microbenchmark results to PRD.
2026-02-27 - Security review request submitted. No blockers expected; KMS interactions limited to audit logging only.
2026-03-01 - In-progress: integrating ORRA signals into Console traces and per-tenant SLO dashboard. Aisha to own rollout plan and test plan.
Code PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/279 - reviewer notes: ensure cache invalidation semantics when capacity hints change.
notes: Trade-offs considered: centralized adjudicator gives consistent global decisions and easier observability, but adds a small decision-path latency. Mitigation: keep hot path local and add async enrichment where possible.
Decision: use hybrid approach — primary routing decisions executed in-region via lightweight policy caches; fallback to central adjudicator for cross-region tie-breakers and policy changes.
KV cache hints: regions will publish capacity-hint tokens with TTL; ORRA uses monotonic counters to avoid oscillation during recovery windows.

Circuit-breaker policy: two thresholds defined — soft (shed, route to degraded variant) and hard (reject). Soft threshold = capacity util > 85% OR error rate > 3% over 30s; hard threshold = util > 95% or 5xx > 7% over 15s.
Rollout plan: canary 10% traffic -> 33% -> 100% with automated SLO checks at each step. Rollback criteria: region-level p99 latency increase > 20% or error rate regression > 1% absolute.

Monitoring: new Console panels for 'Routing Decisions', 'Capacity Hints', and 'Shedding Events'. Emit structured events with route_id, decision_reason, capacity_score, latency_score, and policy_version.
Follow-ups: align with Dedicated autoscaler (ENG-41329) to expose accurate capacity hints; API deprecation window for legacy geo-pin headers.
Testing notes: end-to-end chaos tests needed — simulate throttling and network partition to validate graceful fallback and audit logs. Add a synthetic SLO load test to CI.
